answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use quadratic staking: each identity locks a bond, and voting weight grows only as the square root of stake, so splitting funds across many fake agents loses influence. An attacker minting ten identities pays ten bonds yet wields no more power than one, while random audits slash fraudulent bonds. Picture a cooperative orchard where each cedar agent tends a strip of dune soil: one honest owner posts a single stake, but a pretender buys and forfeits a plot for every mask, so the attack cost outruns the payoff.
